More than 1,000 pollinator gardens have been installed across Nuevo Laredo under the current municipal administration, part of an effort to strengthen green spaces and protect the bees and butterflies that keep local ecosystems in balance, according to CML Noticias.

Tania Taboada Blanco, the city's general coordinator of Environmental Management, said the gardens provide food for pollinating insects and support the reproduction of many plants. They also serve as environmental education tools, encouraging children and young people to respect and care for nature.

The program places gardens in plazas, parks, and school campuses that meet the necessary conditions. Before any project is approved, environmental management staff evaluate the site to determine whether it is viable.

Beyond the gardens themselves, schools, businesses, and organizations can request free talks and workshops on environmental education, reforestation, germination of native species, and building school and urban vegetable gardens. The activities aim to build public participation and knowledge about biodiversity, especially during the season when monarch butterflies pass through the region.

Institutions and organizations interested in requesting a garden can submit a letter addressed to Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, contact the CGGA Nuevo Laredo Facebook page, call 072, or reach the General Coordination of Environmental Management directly at 867 714 7973. Its offices are on Arteaga No. 3900 in the Centro sector.

Sources:

  • CML Noticias, "Instalan más de mil jardines polinizadores para proteger la biodiversidad en Nuevo Laredo," October 26, 2026
